A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SLoPe and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The complete 23-page v1 and 28-page v3 support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT2 and BERT pretraining evaluations, downstream accuracy, runtime and memory measurements, and ablation experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds zero-shot evaluations, FlashAttention-2 comparisons, smaller dense-model controls, and depth-versus-width pruning experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the pruning and optimizer input from gradInput/gradInputSparse to gradWeight/gradWeightSparse. This limited pseudocode correction matches the weight-gradient treatment already described in v1 Section 2.3 and Appendix K; it does not establish a changed experimental implementation. Static double pruning, lazy adapters, tiling and fusion remain.

E1.justification: v3 adds zero-shot evaluations on MMLU, ARC-Challenge, OpenBookQA, WinoGrande, HellaSwag, MathQA, PIQA and RACE (Table 4), plus zero-shot GPT evaluation on GLUE (Appendix Q). v1 evaluated GPT through OpenWebText perplexity and GLUE through fine-tuned BERT. These additions substantially broaden task coverage and transfer scenarios.

E2.justification: v3 adds GPT2-Half as a smaller dense comparator against SLoPe (Tables 13–14), FlashAttention-2 standalone controls (Table 12), and lazy-adapter-augmented Extended SR-STE comparisons (Table 4). These substantively expand the comparison methods. SD-P becoming FST is a rename of the same Hu et al. work, not an additional baseline.

E3.justification: v3 enables FlashAttention-2 in the main systems benchmarks and adds LLaMA-3-8B and Mistral-v0.3-7B configurations. Figure 2 evaluates SR-STE decay factors of 6e-6, 4.5e-4 and 2e-4. New experiments introduce GPT2-Half and half-depth versus half-MLP-width controls for LLaMA-2/Gemma models. These substantially extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: New analyses test FlashAttention-2 compatibility (Appendix M), SR-STE decay sensitivity (Figure 2), adapter benefits for dynamic sparsity, smaller dense-model alternatives (Appendix P), and depth-versus-width pruning (Appendix S, Figure 10). The earlier adapter-rank, mixed-sparsity, module-pruning and kernel ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report median timing over 1,000 iterations and median memory usage over five runs. v3 does not introduce seed reporting, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. Appendix S's statement about no significant difference is qualitative, without a reported statistical procedure.

E6.justification: OPT-13B training/no-adapter inference speedups change from 1.12×/1.30× in v1 Table 1 to 1.25×/1.54× in v3 Table 2, under the changed FlashAttention-2 setup; training memory changes from 0.78 to 0.68. New zero-shot, dense-control, compatibility and pruning results substantially expand findings. The BERT accuracy tables and Appendix L scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the analytical memory accounting, replacing approximate 1.37×/1.83× reductions with explicit terms for duplicated sparse weights, masks, gradients and optimizer states. Lemma 2.1, Theorem 2.2 and their proofs remain substantively unchanged after Appendix O becomes T. The added initialization discussion explains existing assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same three contributions but revise claimed training/inference speedups from 1.14×/1.34× to 1.25×/1.54× and memory ratios from 0.77/0.51 to 0.63/0.61. These are quantitative claim revisions; the later inference-memory headline does not match the retained 0.51 entry in Table 3.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations about compatibility with FlashAttention-2 and adapter benefits for dynamic training. Appendix R explains why final parameter counts limit quality comparisons with FST; Appendix S qualifies width-pruning comparisons because attention parameters remain intact. New dense-control and depth/width findings broaden the discussion, although the claimed consistent zero-shot superiority overlooks MMLU and MathQA exceptions in Table 4.

D1.justification: New Appendix R supplies FST and Extended SR-STE forward/backward code listings, and Tables 15–17 specify pruning-model configurations. v3 also documents the evaluation harness, baseline decay factors and BERT Wanda post-pruning fine-tuning. The latter is additional disclosure, not evidence that retained BERT experiments changed. Existing hardware, training-time and code-access information is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for ARC, MMLU, OpenBookQA, the evaluation harness, Gemma 2 and Llama 2, while removing the AdamW reference. Appendix N further distinguishes SLoPe from sparse-plus-low-rank fine-tuning through backward-pass acceleration and delayed adapter overhead. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose remain. v3 makes localized terminology corrections, expands initialization and baseline explanations, adds a terminology glossary, and inserts new appendix sections while renumbering retained ones. The additional scientific content does not amount to a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds the glossary, zero-shot and compatibility tables, dense-model comparisons, three configuration tables, two code listings and Figure 10. Figure 2 gains decay-specific curves and an expanded legend; systems tables gain model rows. Retained displays are also resized and relocated, with new appendix floats interrupting the proofs.

improvement.justification: v1's GPT evidence centered on perplexity and lacked smaller dense-model and FlashAttention controls. v3 supplies these comparisons, broader downstream evaluations and baseline implementation details, improving the evidence and its transparency. The gain is limited by new overstatements: Table 4 contradicts consistent zero-shot superiority, and Table 3 contradicts the revised inference-memory headline. The revision therefore supports a limited net improvement.
